Hi Hélène, Marissa — following up with the technical details:

1) Regions and Hosted API
- Hosted: we operate an EU region (eu-west-1, deployed in Frankfurt and Dublin availability zones). When a customer selects the EU region endpoints, request processing and storage are kept within the EU by default.
- Cross-region routing: by default our smart routing can fail over between regions for availability; however, for customers with residency requirements we have a routing policy that can be configured to pin traffic to a particular region and disable cross-region failover. That policy is supported for both Hosted (regional endpoints) and Dedicated (reserved pools).

2) Dedicated vs Private
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in the customer’s chosen cloud region (we currently support Dedicated provisioning in eu-west-1). Data processing stays in the selected region; tenancy is isolated at the cluster level. Lead time: typically 3-6 weeks depending on capacity.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network and control plane; data never leaves customer VPC unless explicitly configured. Best for strict residency and audit requirements. Lead time varies (4-8 weeks for VPC integration; on-prem longer).

3) APAC availability
- Hosted APAC region (ap-southeast-1) is scheduled for Q3 2026 (target Aug 2026).
- Dedicated in APAC can be provisioned but will have additional lead time and zone constraints; we can provide a firm timeline once we have a rough sizing.

4) Latency expectations (rough)
- EU-hosted endpoints: 40-80 ms p50 from major EU metros; p95 100-140 ms depending on sequence length and batching.
- APAC -> EU (if using EU endpoints): expect 120-180 ms p50 depending on carrier and routing.

5) Routing/fallbacks
- For customers that require strict residency, we can disable cross-region fallback and configure model routing policies to fall back only to approved EU variants.

Attachment: region-availability.xlsx (region matrix + lead times)

If that aligns with your constraints we can proceed with the tech deep-dive on Thu 6/11 15:00 CET. I’ll bring example architecture diagrams and a short demo of the VPC integration flow.

Hello Hélène — adding a few compliance points from our side: 

- KMS/BYOK: For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) with full control; Dedicated supports BYOK via customer-managed KMS in their cloud account. Hosted (regional) supports server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys; we can also offer customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts with an approved key escrow process.
- Audit artifacts: we can provide SOC2 report (attached), ISO summaries, and architecture diagrams showing data flow and controls.
- Cross-border controls: we enforce region pinning at the routing layer and log all denials/fallbacks. For customers requiring no cross-border processing we sign an addendum that specifies routing and failover behavior; this is enforceable operationally.

Attachments: SOC2-report-2025.pdf, kms-byok-guide.pdf

Happy to join the technical workshop and walk through the attestation language procurement will need.
